summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with acute-on-chronic right upper quadrant abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. Initial imaging including CT abdomen and right upper quadrant ultrasound showed no acute pathology, biliary disease, or obstruction. Labs were stable with no signs of infection or pancreatitis. Diarrhea resolved quickly, followed by constipation likely due to pain medications, which was managed with a bowel regimen including senna and docusate, later supported by a KUB showing fecal loading. Pain was managed with acetaminophen and gabapentin, avoiding opioids due to risk of worsening constipation and lack of clear benefit. The patient improved with dietary advancement, ambulation, and symptom management, understanding that pain may be neuropathic or centrally mediated given absence of structural cause. She was discharged home in stable condition on a regimen including gabapentin, bowel agents, and simethicone, with follow-up planned with chronic pain and primary care.
